| A [`headersHelper`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#trust-a-folder-before-its-headershelper-runs) on a server in `.mcp.json` | Not run until you accept the trust dialog, which appears again naming where the helper is declared. Claude Code connects the server with its static `headers` alone until then | Not run. Claude Code connects the server with its static `headers` alone and prints a [`headersHelper not run`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#headershelper-not-run) line per server to stderr |

For the rows that need this exact folder trusted, trust it by hand: set `projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` to `true` in `~/.claude.json`, where `<path>` is the repository root, or the folder itself outside a repository. Claude Code prints the exact key in the debug log line for a skipped subagent hook or inline MCP server, in the stderr warning for skipped allow rules, and in the `headersHelper not run` line for a skipped helper.

Before you run `claude -p` in a repository you didn't write, decide what it may run on your machine:

* Pass `--setting-sources user`, or set the SDK's `settingSources` without project settings, so Claude Code reads neither the project's settings files nor its `.mcp.json`
* Start with [`--bare`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless#start-faster-with-bare-mode) so Claude Code reads no hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, or `.mcp.json` servers from the project. The project's `env` block and helpers such as `awsAuthRefresh` in its settings files still apply, and Claude Code reads `apiKeyHelper` only from `--settings`
* Pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to [turn hooks off](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md#disable-or-remove-hooks) for that run. Setting it in your user settings alone isn't enough, because the repository's project settings take precedence over yours and can set it back to `false`
* Add a [`disabledMcpjsonServers`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#disabledmcpjsonservers) entry to reject a `.mcp.json` server by name in every session type

lastPrompt: Is there a way to prevent the mode from changing?

content.text:
Partly. There's no setting that stops you switching modes in the middle of a session. But you can turn off the two modes that let me act without asking, and add deny rules that hold whatever mode you're in.

1. **Turn off the risky modes.** The Claude Code permissions docs say to set `permissions.disableAutoMode` and `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` to `"disable"`. They work in any settings file. Auto mode is the one that let me write files in this session.
2. **Add deny rules.** Deny rules are checked before allow rules, from any settings file. They block a tool even in a mode that would otherwise let it run without asking, like accept-edits mode.

For your project's `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "dontAsk",
    "allow": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
    "deny": ["Edit", "Write", "NotebookEdit", "Bash", "PowerShell"],
    "disableAutoMode": "disable",
    "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"
  }
}
```

If you want this for every project, put the same lines in `C:\Users\Creator\.claude\settings.json`. That's your user-level file, and it currently only sets the theme and `defaultMode: "plan"`.

One thing to know: `Edit` and `Write` in the deny list also block me from updating your roadmap file and my notes about you. If you still want me to keep your progress notes updated, use path-specific rules instead of a blanket deny. For example, `Edit(/scenes/**)` and `Write(/scenes/**)` block only your Godot project files.

I haven't changed any settings. Tell me if you want me to add this, or you can paste it in yourself.

message.content: give me the disable for all modes that aren't plan or don't ask.

content.text:
Only two modes have a disable setting, auto and bypass:

```json
"disableAutoMode": "disable",
"disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"
```

Both go inside `"permissions"`. There's no disable setting for the other two modes, manual and accept-edits. You'll still be able to switch to those with Shift+Tab.

Manual mode asks you before every edit or shell command, so it can't do anything you don't approve. Accept-edits mode is the risky one, because it approves file edits automatically. To stop it from editing, add deny rules:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "defaultMode": "dontAsk",
    "allow": ["Read", "Grep", "Glob"],
    "deny": ["Edit", "Write", "NotebookEdit", "Bash", "PowerShell"],
    "disableAutoMode": "disable",
    "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"
  }
}
```

With this config, I can't edit files or run commands in any mode you're able to switch to.

message.content: can I disable those modes too?

content.text:
No, there isn't a setting for that. The docs only have disable switches for auto and bypass, so manual and accept-edits will always be in the Shift+Tab cycle.

The deny rules already make those two modes harmless, though. A deny rule blocks a tool in every mode, so with `Edit`, `Write`, `NotebookEdit`, `Bash` and `PowerShell` denied:

- **Accept-edits mode** has nothing left to approve automatically, because the edit tools are blocked.
- **Manual mode** won't even ask you about those tools. It refuses them, the same as don't-ask mode.

So switching to either one doesn't give me any more access than plan or don't-ask. They're only names you can cycle past.

You could go further with a hook script that checks which mode the session is in before each tool call and blocks anything outside plan or don't-ask. The deny rules already cover what that would do, so I don't think it's worth setting up.

message.content: Is there a way to use my claude subscription without using this harness?

content.text:
Yes. Your subscription also works in the regular Claude apps, which aren't Claude Code:

- **claude.ai** in a browser
- **The Claude desktop app** for Windows (its normal chat, not the Code tab)
- **The Claude mobile apps**

For your learning setup, plain chat is a good fit. I can't touch your files there at all. You paste in your script or attach it, and I review it and give hints. There's nothing to configure and no modes to worry about.

A few things don't count as getting away from this harness:

- **The VS Code and JetBrains extensions, claude.ai/code, and the desktop app's Code tab** all run Claude Code. They use the same permission settings and modes.
- **The Claude API** is billed separately from your subscription. Using it in other tools means buying API credits.
- **Third-party coding tools** usually need an API key rather than your subscription login. Check each tool's own rules before assuming your plan covers it.

If you stay in Claude Code, the deny rules from before are what keep me read-only. In the regular chat apps, I can't edit your project at all.

content.text:
# Keybindings Skill

Create or modify `~/.claude/keybindings.json` to customize keyboard shortcuts.

## CRITICAL: Read Before Write

**Always read `~/.claude/keybindings.json` first** (it may not exist yet). Merge changes with existing bindings — never replace the entire file.

- Use **Edit** tool for modifications to existing files
- Use **Write** tool only if the file does not exist yet

## File Format

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-keybindings.json",
  "$docs": "https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings",
  "bindings": [
    {
      "context": "Chat",
      "bindings": {
        "ctrl+e": "chat:externalEditor"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Always include the `$schema` and `$docs` fields.

## Keystroke Syntax

**Modifiers** (combine with `+`):
- `ctrl` (alias: `control`)
- `alt` (aliases: `opt`, `option`) — note: `alt` and `meta` are identical in terminals
- `shift`
- `meta` — same key as `alt` in terminals (Option key on macOS)
- `cmd` (aliases: `command`, `super`, `win`) — Command key on macOS, Windows key on Windows, Super key on Linux; not the same as `meta`. Most terminals never send it (only ones that report the Super modifier, such as through the Kitty keyboard protocol or xterm `modifyOtherKeys`), so prefer `ctrl` for bindings that should work everywhere

**Special keys**: `escape`/`esc`, `enter`/`return`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`

**Chords**: Space-separated keystrokes, e.g. `ctrl+k ctrl+s` (3-second timeout between keystrokes)

**Examples**: `ctrl+shift+p`, `alt+enter`, `ctrl+k ctrl+n`

## Unbinding Default Shortcuts

Set a key to `null` to remove its default binding:

```json
{
  "context": "Chat",
  "bindings": {
    "ctrl+s": null
  }
}
```

## How User Bindings Interact with Defaults

- User bindings are **additive** — they are appended after the default bindings
- To **move** a binding to a different key: unbind the old key (`null`) AND add the new binding
- A context only needs to appear in the user's file if they want to change something in that context

## Common Patterns

### Rebind a key
To change the external editor shortcut from `ctrl+g` to `ctrl+e`:
```json
{
  "context": "Chat",
  "bindings": {
    "ctrl+g": null,
    "ctrl+e": "chat:externalEditor"
  }
}
```

### Add a chord binding
```json
{
  "context": "Global",
  "bindings": {
    "ctrl+k ctrl+t": "app:toggleTodos"
  }
}
```

## Behavioral Rules

1. Only include contexts the user wants to change (minimal overrides)
2. Validate that actions and contexts are from the known lists below
3. Warn the user proactively if they choose a key that conflicts with reserved shortcuts or common tools like tmux (`ctrl+b`) and screen (`ctrl+a`)
4. When adding a new binding for an existing action, the new binding is additive (existing default still works unless explicitly unbound)
5. To fully replace a default binding, unbind the old key AND add the new one

## Validation

Claude Code validates `~/.claude/keybindings.json` when it loads; warnings go to the debug log. After editing the file, re-check it against the rules below and fix anything that matches.

### Common Issues and Fixes

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keybindings.json must have a "bindings" array` | Missing wrapper object | Wrap bindings in `{ "bindings": [...] }` |
| `"bindings" must be an array` | `bindings` is not an array | Set `"bindings"` to an array: `[{ context: ..., bindings: ... }]` |
| `Unknown context "X"` | Typo or invalid context name | Use exact context names from the Available Contexts table |
| `"X" is not a modifier, so the binding "Y" ... is ignored` | Error: `X` comes before the key in `Y` but is not a modifier (a typo such as `ctl` for `ctrl`, or two keys joined with `+` instead of a space), so the binding is ignored and every key keeps its current action | Correct the modifier using the Keystroke Syntax list (the message suggests the corrected keystroke when it can), or put a space between the keystrokes of a chord |
| `Duplicate key "X" in Y bindings` | Same key defined twice in one context | Remove the duplicate; JSON uses only the last value |
| `"X" may not work: ...` | Key conflicts with terminal/OS reserved shortcut | Choose a different key (see Reserved Shortcuts section) |
| `Invalid action for "X"` | Action value is not a string or null | Actions must be strings like `"app:help"` or `null` to unbind |

### Example validation warnings (debug log)

```
[keybindings] Found 2 validation issue(s)
[keybindings] [error] Unknown context "chat" — Valid contexts: Global, Chat, Autocomplete, ...
[keybindings] [warning] "ctrl+c" may not work: Terminal interrupt (SIGINT)
```

**Errors** mean some or all of your bindings are ignored or don't work as written, and must be fixed. **Warnings** indicate potential conflicts but the binding may still work.

## Reserved Shortcuts

### Non-rebindable (errors)
- `ctrl+c` — Cannot be rebound - used for interrupt/exit (hardcoded)
- `ctrl+d` — Cannot be rebound - used for exit (hardcoded)
- `ctrl+m` — Cannot be rebound - identical to Enter in terminals (both send CR)
- `ctrl+[` — Cannot be rebound - identical to Escape in terminals
- `ctrl+i` — Cannot be rebound - identical to Tab in terminals
- `ctrl+h` — Cannot be rebound - identical to Backspace in terminals
- `capslock` — Caps Lock is not delivered to terminal applications

### Terminal reserved (errors/warnings)
- `ctrl+z` — Unix process suspend (SIGTSTP) (may conflict)
- `ctrl+\` — Terminal quit signal (SIGQUIT) (will not work)

### macOS reserved (errors)
- `cmd+c` — macOS system copy
- `cmd+v` — macOS system paste
- `cmd+x` — macOS system cut
- `cmd+q` — macOS quit application
- `cmd+w` — macOS close window/tab
- `cmd+tab` — macOS app switcher
- `cmd+space` — macOS Spotlight

## Available Contexts

| Context | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Global` | Active everywhere, regardless of focus |
| `Chat` | When the chat input is focused |
| `Autocomplete` | When autocomplete menu is visible |
| `Confirmation` | When a confirmation/permission dialog is shown |
| `Help` | When the help overlay is open |
| `Transcript` | When viewing the transcript |
| `HistorySearch` | When searching command history (ctrl+r) |
| `Task` | When a task/agent is running in the foreground |
| `ThemePicker` | When the theme picker is open |
| `Settings` | When the settings menu is open |
| `Tabs` | When tab navigation is active |
| `Attachments` | When navigating image attachments in a select dialog |
| `Footer` | When footer indicators are focused |
| `AbovePrompt` | When a plugin's panel above the prompt, or a button in it, has keyboard focus |
| `AbovePromptInput` | When a plugin's input field above the prompt has keyboard focus |
| `AbovePromptSelect` | When a plugin's select above the prompt has keyboard focus |
| `Pane` | When a plugin's pane has keyboard focus |
| `PaneField` | When an input field or select in a plugin's pane has keyboard focus |
| `MessageSelector` | When the message selector (rewind) is open |
| `DiffDialog` | When the diff dialog is open |
| `DiffPanel` | When the diff sidebar panel is open |
| `ModelPicker` | When the model picker is open |
| `EffortSlider` | When the effort slider is open |
| `Select` | When a select/list component is focused |
| `Plugin` | When the plugin dialog is open |
| `Scroll` | When a scrollable view is focused (fullscreen layout) |
| `Agents` | When the agents view (`claude agents`) is open |

## Available Actions

| Action | Default Key(s) | Context |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app:interrupt` | `ctrl+c` | Global |
| `app:exit` | `ctrl+d` | Global |
| `app:toggleTodos` | `ctrl+t` | Global |
| `app:toggleTranscript` | `ctrl+o` | Global |
| `app:toggleBrief` | `ctrl+shift+b` | Global |
| `app:toggleReplTab` | (none) | Global |
| `app:toggleDiffNoiseFilter` | (none) | Global |
| `app:diffFileListUp` | `ctrl+up`, `meta+up` | Global |
| `app:diffFileListDown` | `ctrl+down`, `meta+down` | Global |
| `app:toggleDiffPreSession` | (none) | Global |
| `app:cycleDiffBase` | `ctrl+x b` | DiffPanel |
| `app:closeSession` | (none) | Global |
| `app:toggleTerminal` | (none) | Global |
| `app:redraw` | (none) | Global |
| `app:openArtifact` | `ctrl+]` | Global |
| `history:search` | `ctrl+r` | Global |
| `history:previous` | `up` | Chat |
| `history:next` | `down` | Chat |
| `chat:cancel` | `escape` | Chat |
| `chat:killAgents` | `ctrl+x ctrl+k` | Chat |
| `chat:cycleMode` | `shift+tab` | Chat |
| `chat:modelPicker` | `meta+p` | Chat |
| `chat:increaseEffort` | `ctrl+x ctrl+=`, `ctrl+x =`, `shift+up` | Chat |

message.content: is claude able to change my mode?

content.text:
Not on its own. There are two things I can do that touch modes:

- **Enter plan mode.** I can switch the session into plan mode without asking you. Plan mode only makes things stricter, so that can't give me more access.
- **Ask to leave plan mode.** Leaving plan mode shows you an approval prompt, and the prompt lets you choose which mode comes next. This is probably how this session ended up in auto mode: the conversation began with a note that plan mode had been exited and auto mode was active. Nothing changes until you pick an option there.

The other route would be editing your settings files, such as changing `defaultMode` in `.claude/settings.json`. That needs Edit, Write, Bash or PowerShell, and your deny list blocks all four once you add it.

The weak point is the leave-plan-mode prompt, since that's where auto mode can get picked. Your setup covers it. With `disableAutoMode` set, auto mode can't be chosen from that prompt. With the deny rules, the modes that are still available can't edit anything.

message.content: but if you goto plan mode I can't get back to dontAsk

content.text:
You're right, and the keybinding change makes it worse. Unbinding Shift+Tab also takes away your own way to switch modes. Here are the ways back:

- **Restart the session.** A new session starts in your `defaultMode`, which is `dontAsk`. This one is guaranteed to work.
- **Rebind mode switching to a key you won't hit by accident.** Instead of only unbinding Shift+Tab, give `chat:cycleMode` a two-step shortcut so you can still switch on purpose:
  ```json
  {
    "context": "Chat",
    "bindings": {
      "shift+tab": null,
      "ctrl+x m": "chat:cycleMode"
    }
  }
  ```
  You'd press Ctrl+X, then M.

One thing I'm not sure about: I don't think don't-ask mode is in the Shift+Tab cycle at all. As far as I know, the cycle goes manual → accept-edits → plan, with auto added if it's enabled. Don't-ask comes from `defaultMode` or the command-line flag. If that's right, restarting is the only way to get it back once you leave it, whatever the keybinding.

With your deny rules in place, landing in manual mode isn't a problem. Edits and commands are blocked there exactly as in don't-ask. The only difference is that for tools you haven't allowed or denied, like web fetches, manual mode asks you instead of refusing.

message.content: but you can't cycle into dontAsk...

content.text:
Right, so once a session leaves don't-ask mode, the only way back is to restart it.

You can stop me from leaving don't-ask in the first place. Entering plan mode is a tool I call, named `EnterPlanMode`, and deny rules work on tools by name. Add it to your deny list:

```json
"deny": ["Edit", "Write", "NotebookEdit", "Bash", "PowerShell", "EnterPlanMode"]
```

Then the only way out of don't-ask mode is you pressing the mode-switch key.

I haven't seen this used on `EnterPlanMode` specifically, so test it once. Start a new session and ask me to enter plan mode. If the call is refused, the rule works.
